Docs.summary: Application-wide factory for creating instances. Register an implementation in the application's to replace the built-in modal presentation for each window the factory chooses to handle.

remarks.para: When an is present in for a window, the framework calls once for that window and routes every modal push and pop to the returned instance instead of the built-in platform code. This lets alternative platform backends render modal navigation without reflection, partial classes or forking, while the framework keeps ownership of the cross-platform modal stack, the page lifecycle events and the push/pop reconciliation loop.

The factory is resolved from the window's service scope, so it may be registered with any lifetime. The framework calls it once per window and disposes the returned instance, so return a new for each call. It is called again for the same window only if the window gets a new handler, which brings a new service scope (for example an Android activity recreation).

If this method throws, the framework logs the exception and permanently falls back to the built-in platform for that window rather than rethrowing from whatever call site happened to trigger resolution. Creation is not retried, so a failed registration fails deterministically and visibly in the log instead of throwing repeatedly from arbitrary navigation code. Prefer returning over throwing when a backend deliberately does not want to handle a window.

Public Function CreateModalNavigationPlatform (host As IModalNavigationHost) As IModalNavigationPlatform

Docs.param: The per-window host that exposes the framework's modal navigation state. Keep a reference to it; it stays valid for the lifetime of the returned instance.
Docs.returns: A new owned and disposed by the framework, or to let the window keep the built-in platform implementation. Returning is useful when a backend only wants to override modal navigation for certain windows.
